A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATA research. Their main texts, equations, algorithms, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original task-allocation and SGD simulations, runtime and worker-time comparisons in Tables 1–2, and repeated regret simulations in Section 7.2.

after.justification: V2 retains those results and adds heterogeneous timing-distribution simulations, CIFAR-100 training results and experiments varying prior timing observations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Equations (7)–(8) change the confidence multipliers from 4eα and 4eξ to 2α and 2η. ATA uses a centered Orlicz-norm bound, while ATA-Empirical replaces standard-deviation/mean prior information with an Orlicz-norm/mean bound. These change confidence calculations, but the allocation objective, algorithm loop and RAS procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic quadratic optimization and timing simulations. V2 adds CNN training on CIFAR-100 and a distinct worker environment combining Exponential, Uniform, Half-Normal, Lognormal and Gamma timing distributions, substantially broadening task and environment coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain GTA/Rennala SGD, OFTA, labelled FTA: Optimal in plots, and UTA. V2 extends the same comparator set to its new experiments. Adam is the CNN optimizer, not an added allocation baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 introduces a 160k-parameter CNN evaluated with Adam at learning rate 8×10^-5, B=23 and n=17, 51, 153. Appendix A.5 adds a controlled protocol using 0, 500,000 or 5,000,000 prior bandit iterations at n=51. These are new experimental designs; the retained synthetic settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds robustness tests across five timing-distribution families with matched means within worker groups. Appendix A.5 tests how prior timing observations reduce exploration costs, a benefit only discussed in v1. The original linear-noise and regret analyses are retained as A.1 and A.3.

E5.justification: The regret experiment still reports five simulation runs and standard-deviation bars: v1 Section 7.2/Figure 3 becomes v2 Appendix A.3/Figure 4. No new repeated-run counts, seed disclosures or uncertainty-reporting procedures accompany the added experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original plots are retained, including the regret plot renumbered from Figure 3 to Figure 4. New Figures 3, 5 and 6 report mixed-distribution behavior, CIFAR-100 loss versus runtime and worker time, and faster approach to OFTA with prior observations. These are additional outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1 changes to centered Orlicz norms. Theorem 4.2 replaces 1+η√ln(B) with 1+4ηln(B), with η redefined through Orlicz norms. Theorem 6.3 replaces the factor (1+η²)α_i² with η²μ_i². V1's variance-to-Orlicz lemma is removed, and v2 substantially revises concentration, maximum and regret proofs in Appendices D–E.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement retain the same claims: adaptive allocation without knowing worker means, performance comparable to informed allocation, resource savings over greedy allocation, and the ATA-Empirical variant. The revised mathematical guarantees and additional experiments do not change these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 now explains ATA-Empirical's adaptivity through η²μ_i² and relates recovery of individual Orlicz-norm dependence to comparable α_i/μ_i ratios across workers. V1 presented individual-norm adaptation without this qualification. Appendix A.2 also adds an interpretation of the new results as robustness across timing distributions.

D1.justification: V2 supplies sampling formulas for the new timing distributions, CNN layer and parameter counts, the Adam learning rate, and the procedure for reusing prior bandit observations. The existing Python and Intel Xeon implementation disclosure moves to Appendix A; no code-access resource is added.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Boucheron et al. for concentration results, Kingma and Ba for Adam, and Krizhevsky et al. for CIFAR. The related-work positioning is otherwise retained. Updated MindFlayer and Ringmaster publication information refers to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain unchanged. The linear-noise and regret subsections move into a new experimental appendix, subsequent appendices are relabelled, and v2 adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Heading capitalization, correspondence information and several explanations receive limited editing.

P2.justification: V2 adds three substantial multipanel figures for heterogeneous distributions, CIFAR-100 and prior observations. Existing Figure 2 and the regret figure move into the appendix, with the latter becoming Figure 4. Table 2 is widened and expands method labels. The new displays and redistribution substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens theoretical and empirical support. Appendix E replaces v1's problematic variance-based maximum and norm arguments with explicit Orlicz-norm derivations, while Appendix A adds a real neural-network task and targeted robustness and exploration studies. These address important weaknesses of v1. The runtime guarantee becomes weaker, and centered versus uncentered norm definitions remain inconsistent, so the improvement is in support and validation rather than a stronger guarantee.
